newsitem.title: INDIA: JNOC offers farm-in prospects to ONGC.
newsitem.headline: JNOC offers farm-in prospects to ONGC.

text.p: State-owned Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) has offered farm-in rights to India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp in existing oilfields abroad, a senior ONGC official said on Wednesday.
"JNOC is getting concessions in Indonesia, Australia, Oman and Egypt. They are willing to consider it if ONGC Videsh ltd (OVL) wants to farm-in with them in these areas," the official said.
An OVL team will leave for Tokyo next month to study the data on the oilfields, he said.

OVL, a wholly-owned subsidiary of ONGC, is pursuing opportunities for acquiring equity oil abroad. Its mandate was recently expanded to include production and development activities in addition to overseas exploration.
During talks with ONGC officials on Tuesday, the JNOC delegation also expressed interest in joining hands with ONGC in oil exploration in deep water areas beyond 400 metres bathymetry, he said.
"They have indicated their willingness to join hands with ONGC on deep water oil exploration projects. For other oilfields (in India), they are thinking of exploring on their own."

Under a revised global strategy, JNOC plans to raise its share of equity oil to 30 percent of imports from 10 percent. The thrust will be to increase share through joint ventures abroad, the JNOC delegation told Indian officials on Monday.
The Japanese company has been investing in oil exploration projects to gain crude as profit for their share of equity. It has 120 exploration ventures so far of which 40 are producing areas.

The JNOC delegation, led by vice-president Mineo Kinoshita, also held talks with officials of ONGC, Oil India ltd, Gas Authority of India ltd, Indian Oil Corp and India's Petroleum Ministry on Monday.
During the meeting, the delegation told their Indian counterparts of their methods of evaluating seismic data dockets and submitting bids.
